MANILA, Philippines — Rollbacks are expected for gasoline, diesel and kerosene next week as the price of fuel continues to drop in the world market.
Based on the three-day Mean of Platts Singapore trading, the following reductions are expected:
Price declines were dampened in previous weeks by fears that the US may strike Iran. However, the Democratic party's gains in the American Senate and Congress at their midterm elections earlier this week countered these concerns, even after President Donald Trump ordered a strike on Iran's Qeshm Island.
The landslide victory allows the opposition to stop appointments, launch investigations and block legislation, including provisions that support Trump's war against Iran.
The Philippine peso also recovered to a P62:$1 trading level, closing at P62.97 on Thursday, November 5.
A higher exchange rate is linked to higher fuel prices because dollars are the currency used to purchase crude.
Higher fuel and transport costs pushed inflation to a three-year record high of 7.8% in October.
The country remains on a tightening cycle to manage inflation, but the central bank maintains that its monetary policy at present is not intended to support a particular exchange rate.

This aptly described the wrong coordinates on the sites of farm-to-market-roads (FMR) that went into the final print of the proposed 2027 General Appropriations Bill). In particular, the Department of Agriculture (DA) found out the wrong coordinates affected only eight (8) out of the 1,669 FMR projects listed in the National Expenditure Program (NEP) under the 2027 GAB.
In our Kapihan sa Manila Bay last Wednesday, DA official spokesman Arnel de Mesa disclosed the eight FMR projects with wrong geo-tag coordinates were discovered belatedly by the DA upon review. When people hear politicians talk about a “politics of love,” the reaction is usually a big roll of the eyes. Mine included. In a world full of nasty political fights, toxic internet arguments, and multi-million-dollar attack ads, bringing up “love” sounds like a weak, soft idea meant for self-help books – not government policy.
But a real politics of love isn’t about giving out warm hugs or pretending everyone agrees. It is a tough, practical blueprint for running a fair society. To understand why it works, we don’t have to look at modern political spin; we can look at the most famous disruption of power in human history: the radical love of Jesus.

Upon returning from our 5-week vacation in the EU, friends watched the chaos, riots, and looting that happened in many parts of Europe particularly in Paris, France and they could not help but ask, “How was Paris?”.
People with travel plans to the continent are concerned for their safety and fear that they might get trapped between students rioting and the French police. Others were merely interested to know if all the online videos on snatchers and pickpockets were true.
My honest answer was that I saw people chasing 2 snatchers in Binondo last Nov. 2, I watched the video of 5 robbers shooting it out with cops in Cavite the other day and read about the billions of pesos being shamelessly directed for the political benefit of several congressmen. But not in Paris.
